Connor —

Thanks for the quick call this morning. As we discussed on the Helios side, procurement and legal need an addendum to the MSA that clearly ties capacity activation (top-up pools / burst) to measurable acceptance triggers and an evidence checklist the customer can use during implementation. Two asks from our side:

1) Add language describing "trigger-based activation" (what events let us draw additional committed capacity, e.g., sustained 95th percentile throughput for X days OR a product launch event).
2) An evidence matrix: a short list of artifacts Helios will provide to prove the trigger was met (traffic reports, synthetic test results, onboarding signoffs).

We prefer to keep the core SOW unchanged, but want the addendum to be clear on invoice timing when triggers fire (billing start date, proration), and acceptance criteria for the implementation window. Can you propose redlines and an evidence matrix we can review? Procurement would like a target turnaround of 3 business days.

Attaching our internal draft of the evidence points for reference (we will share the procurement PO after signoff).

Best,
Maya

Maya / procurement team —

Attached are the initial redlines to the MSA (file: Helios_MSA_Addendum_redline_20270420.docx) and a one-page activation-evidence matrix (activation-evidence-matrix_v1.xlsx). Key legal points called out in-line:

1) Trigger definition — we propose two mutually exclusive trigger paths:
   - Operational trigger: sustained 95th percentile token throughput for 72 hours across the advertised endpoints.
   - Event trigger: documented launch event with pre-registered traffic forecast >= X concurrent requests for Y minutes and written confirmation from Helios product ops.

2) Billing/proration — billing for additional committed capacity will start at 00:00 UTC on the calendar day following confirmation that trigger evidence has been accepted. If Helios disputes the evidence within the 7-day acceptance window, billing is paused until resolution; if dispute is resolved in Redwood's favor, billing will be retroactive to that start date (with a single credit for any double-billed day if applicable).

3) Implementation acceptance window — 7 calendar days for verification, during which Redwood will work to remediate configuration issues. Post-window, any remaining defects fall under normal SLAs. We added explicit language limiting the scope of "go-live" checks to artifacts listed in the evidence matrix to avoid open-ended testing obligations.

4) Limited liability / indemnity linkage — we explicitly avoid tying indemnity exposure to trigger events; legal flagged risk if we allow trigger activation to change core indemnity or data processing terms. If Helios wants tighter linkage, please add that to the redlines so we can evaluate.

Attachment stubs: Helios_MSA_Addendum_redline_20270420.docx (tracked changes), activation-evidence-matrix_v1.xlsx (rows: artifact, owner, format, minimum threshold).

- Maya / Helios legal: please review the tracked changes and matrix and flag must-haves by EOD Monday (3 business days per your procurement ask).
- Connor / Laura / Ops: confirm the operational thresholds and how Redwood will validate synthetic tests / logs.

Connor — happy for you to reword any of the commercial bullets prior to sending.

Thanks,
